subject.title: fix(sqlite): allow verified shared wal backports

question: Should OpenClaw support an operator-asserted environment override for the WAL-corruption guard when a shared system SQLite backport cannot be identified from its upstream version?
rationale: Source inspection can assess the implementation, but only maintainers can accept the long-term configuration and data-integrity policy of letting an environment assertion override this guard.

options.title: Keep a guarded override
options.body: Accept the shared-library-only escape hatch after adding an explicit startup warning, operator documentation, focused tests, and real affected-image proof.

options.title: Require machine-verifiable safety
options.body: Do not add the environment variable; instead require a reliable source-ID, package attestation, or maintained distro allowlist before bypassing the guard.

options.title: Keep the strict version gate
options.body: Reject backport exceptions and require operators to install a SQLite build whose reported upstream version is accepted.

recommendation.title: Keep a guarded override
recommendation.body: Accept the shared-library-only escape hatch after adding an explicit startup warning, operator documentation, focused tests, and real affected-image proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent Node installation work is directly connected to the runtime combination that exposed this regression.
